title: Immutable Audit Trail for Regulatory Compliance
business: Financial institutions managing high-stakes transaction ledgers that require non-repudiation.
problem: Mutable state allows for accidental or malicious modification of historical transaction records, leading to audit failures and loss of data integrity.
solution: By enforcing immutability, the system ensures that once a transaction record is constructed and committed to the ledger, its state cannot be altered, providing a reliable source of truth.
steps: Define a data structure with final fields that are initialized only through the constructor.
Remove all setter methods to prevent post-construction modification.
Implement a copy-on-write pattern if a modified version of the data is required.
Serialize the immutable object to a write-once storage medium to finalize the audit trail.
outcome: The system achieves a verifiable and tamper-evident history of all financial activities, simplifying regulatory reporting and internal auditing.
limitation: Immutability increases memory overhead because every state change requires creating a new object instance rather than modifying the existing one. This can be monitored by tracking heap allocation frequency during high-volume transaction periods.
